history.dynasty: Local Nawabi-era (Sidhout Taluk) tradition; shrine complex built up over ~300 years
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Ameen Peer Dargah (locally Pedda Dargah / Badi Dargah; formally the Asthana-e-Magdoom Ilahi complex) in Nakkash Colony, Kadapa, is a Sufi Muslim shrine housing the mausoleums of Sufi saints Peerullah Hussaini and Arufulla Hussaini II. Local lore: Peerullah Hussaini, said to be a descendant of Prophet Muhammad, came south from Ajmer at a divine direction and stopped on the Pennar river banks, where Sidhout Taluk's Nawab Nek Naam Khan paid him homage and, at the saint's request, named the place 'Nek Naam Abaad' - which became Kadapa (the dargah is thus woven into the town's naming tradition). It is called the 'South Ajmer Dargah' and a symbol of communal harmony, visited by people of all faiths including celebrities such as A.R. Rahman (frequenting it since ~2005), Indira Gandhi and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy per local press. Descendants of the saints still serve at the shrine; male devotees wear saffron caps. name: Ameen Peer Dargah
town_description: Kadapa (Cuddapah) is a city in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, headquarters of YSR Kadapa district, on the banks of the Pennar river. A historic town with medieval and Nawabi layers, it is known for the Devuni Kadapa Venkateswara temple, the Ameen Peer Dargah (a symbol of communal harmony), and its long-standing Sufi tradition.
